title_en: JL and Jessica Collins: She Followed Her Dad’s Investing Advice. Then Quit the Job She Hated
title_zh: JL 与 Jessica Collins：她听从爸爸的投资建议，然后辞掉了自己讨厌的工作
subtitle_zh: 畅销书 The Simple Path to Wealth 作者父女对谈：高储蓄、4%法则与提前退休买回自由
summary_zh: 本期 Morningstar 播客 The Long View 由 Christine Benz 与 Amy Arnott 共同主持，嘉宾是畅销书 The Simple Path to Wealth 的作者 JL Collins 及其女儿、配套练习册 The Simple Path to Wealth Workbook 的作者 Jessica Collins。Jessica 从小听爸爸讲理财却提不起兴趣，后来在企业界做 B2B 软件销售，靠持续储蓄工资的50%并投资美国全市场指数基金（index funds），在32岁实现财务独立（financial independence），并在想通一年后辞掉了并不喜欢的工作。JL 认为4%法则（4% rule）极其保守：Trinity study 显示5%的提取率也有约86%的成功率（4%约为96%），因此面对摧残灵魂的工作，他宁可押注86%也要辞职，缺口可用 barista FIRE（咖啡师 FIRE）等方式每年补上1万美元。父女俩都认为对投资缺乏兴趣反而是超能力，能避免瞎折腾组合。JL 还罕见松口：受 Trump 关税政策重塑全球贸易格局影响，他如今也持有了一些全球股票指数基金 VT，但仍主要投资并看多美国市场；他重申房子是生活方式选择而非投资，并对借债读大学持谨慎态度。本集是理解'简单路径'如何落地、以及两代人财务观念差异的生动样本。

turns.zh: 而当我意识到，所有的激进储蓄、真正的勤勉和坚持、以及在金钱上做出的正确选择都已经有了回报时，我才有了那个念头：“哦，好，我可以离开了。”然后，在我意识到自己可以离开的一年之后，我才真正离开。

turns.en: that had chosen me, there'd be something along the lines of, you know, I have, say, a million dollars invested and using the 4% rule that suggests that that'll throw off $40,000 a year that you can live on and you can expect the portfolio to survive. turns.zh: “你看，比如说我有100万美元的投资，按照4%法则，这意味着每年能产生4万美元供我生活，而且可以预期这个组合能撑住。”然后他们会说：“可是我一年需要5万美元”——那就是5%的提取率，超过了那个4%——

turns.en: but I'm in this sole crushing job, what do I do? And my response to that question was always, I'd quit that job yesterday. For a couple of reasons, you are very well positioned at that point. You know, you do have a million dollars. These are mostly young people who have a lot of flexibility to do things going forward.
turns.zh: “但我现在这份工作在摧残我的灵魂，我该怎么办？”我对这个问题的回答永远是：“我昨天就该辞掉那份工作。”原因有几个：在那个节点上你的处境其实非常好。要知道，你手上确实有100万美元。这些人大多还很年轻，未来做事有很大的弹性。

turns.en: If you look at the Trinity study, which explored the 4% idea in further depth, you find that a 5% withdrawal rate succeeds if memory served me 86% of the time. turns.zh: 如果你去看 Trinity study——它对4%的想法做了更深入的研究——你会发现，如果我没记错，5%的提取率有86%的成功概率，而4%我记得是96%。所以86%仍然是很高的胜算。如果是我，处在一份摧残灵魂的工作里，我愿意为这86%掷一次骰子。

turns.en: And then the other thing I would say to those people is, do you think there is something you could figure out to do during the course of the next 12 months after you quit your corporate job that would throw off an extra 10 grand a year to make up the gap?
turns.zh: 然后我还会对这些人说另一句话：你觉得在你辞掉公司工作之后的12个月里，有没有可能想办法做点什么，每年多挣出1万美元来补上这个缺口？

turns.en: And I never once had anybody, when they were asked that question, say, no, I don't think I could do that. Again, people who choose to walk this path, they're smart, engage creative, successful people. turns.zh: 当我问出这个问题时，从来没有一个人回答：“不，我觉得我做不到。”同样，选择走这条路的人，都是聪明、投入、有创意、成功的人。所以说他们想不出办法多挣一点钱来补上缺口，这种想法其实挺可笑的。

turns.en: So there's a lot of flexibility around this 4% rule. And I hesitate on the word rule because I've never been comfortable with it. I think of it as a wonderful guy line. And even Bingen, I think I'm pronouncing his name correctly, I came up with the ideas now saying that that's too conservative.
turns.zh: 所以围绕这个4%法则其实有很大的弹性。我对“法则”这个词很谨慎，因为我一直对它不太舒服。我更愿意把它看作一条很棒的参考线。甚至连 Bengen——我想我名字发音没错——就是提出这个想法的人，现在也说这个标准太保守了，

turns.en: And people can be more generous with their withdrawal rates. And he himself, when he created it, and this is something that I've tried to drum home and my writings and conversations, the 4% that he came up with originally is extraordinarily conservative.

turns.zh: 非常有创意的看待方式，你提到的 barista FIRE 就是一个很好的例子：你辞掉高压工作，也许做一份兼职，挣出一点刚好够维持收支的额外收入，那就挺好。然后还有，你知道，有 lean FIRE（节俭版 FIRE）和 fat FIRE（富足版 FIRE），

turns.en: There are all kinds of different ways to approach this that I think is wonderful to see that creativity come to play. So JL, can you talk about why then when Jess was saying that she was ready to leave her corporate job? Why you didn't think that that was such a great idea?
turns.zh: 还有各种各样不同的做法，我觉得看到这种创造力迸发出来真的很棒。那么 JL，你能谈谈吗——当 Jess 说她准备离开公司工作时，为什么你觉得那不是个特别好的主意？

turns.en: Yeah, so I think that's a reflection of me and my experience in my background coming to the fore without thinking through how different her situation is. So what I mean by that is as we discussed earlier, you know, I wandered in the wilderness for 40 years trying to figure this stuff out.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得那反映的是我本人的经历和背景占了上风，而没有仔细想过她的处境有多么不同。我的意思是，就像我们前面谈到的，我在“旷野”里摸索了40年才弄明白这些东西。

turns.en: And that meant that when I was 32, you know, I was not financially independent and, you know, I had to keep working. There was no other option. And I enjoyed my career, not because it was a great glamorous career, but it was one of those things that, okay, I have to do something during the living.
turns.zh: 这意味着我32岁的时候，并没有实现财务独立，我必须继续工作，没有别的选择。而且我享受我的职业生涯——不是因为它多么光鲜了不起，而是它属于这样一种事情：“好吧，活着总得做点什么谋生，

turns.en: So I'm going to pick something that pays me relatively well and I'm going to be the best that I possibly can be at doing it. And that creates a certain satisfaction. And so I enjoyed my career. So at this young age, she was stepping away. I was a little concerned is she going to give up that enjoyment?
turns.zh: 那我就挑一件报酬相对不错的事，并且尽可能把它做到最好。”这会带来某种满足感。所以我是享受我的职业生涯的。而她在这么年轻的年纪就要抽身离开，我当时有点担心：她是不是要放弃这种工作带来的乐趣？

turns.en: And then the other thing, frankly, is, you know, my perspective on the job she had in her is different because the job she had from my perspective just seemed awesome. I mean, she worked from home. She set her own hours. She got paid commission. She was extraordinarily good at doing it.
turns.zh: 然后还有一点，坦白说，我对她那份工作的看法和她自己不一样，因为在我看来，她那份工作简直棒极了：她在家办公，自己安排时间，拿佣金，而且做得极其出色。

turns.en: And so she made a lot of money and it didn't seem to take that much effort on her part to do this. I'm saying, why would I would never have given up a job like that? But on the other hand, you know, you have to sit back and realize that that's the power
turns.zh: 所以她赚了很多钱，而且看起来并没费她多大力气。我当时想：为什么要辞职？换成我，我绝不会放弃那样的工作。但另一方面，你也得退后一步意识到，这正是

turns.en: of the simple path I created, even though I never got to walk it myself, that, you know, she could do this for a decade and suddenly be in this position where even objectively having a really good job, they just wasn't working for it and she didn't have to do it anymore. That's my defense and I think I came around pretty quickly.
turns.zh: 我创造的这条“简单路径”的力量——尽管我自己从没机会走它：她这样做了十年，忽然就到了这样一个位置——即使客观上她有一份非常好的工作，但这份工作对她来说已经不合适了，而她可以不必再做下去。这就是我的辩解，而且我想我很快就转过弯来了。

turns.en: But it did for all those reasons, it took me a minute. And by, by the way, sitting here now, I think she absolutely made the right decision among other things. She wouldn't have been able to help with the new addition of simple path to wealth and she did a lot of heavy lifting on that with my publisher.
turns.zh: 但确实，因为前面那些原因，我缓了一会儿才接受。顺便说一句，现在坐在这里，我认为她绝对做出了正确的决定。别的不说，如果没辞职，她就没办法帮忙做 The Simple Path to Wealth 的新版，而她在这件事上和我的出版商一起干了很多重活。

turns.en: And of course, the workbook that she just finished writing wouldn't exist had she stayed on that corporate path. So when you leave, you know, your traditional career, when you're able to do that, suddenly all these other opportunities tend to present themselves in unexpected ways.
turns.zh: 当然，她刚刚写完的这本练习册，如果她还留在那条企业轨道上，也根本不会存在。所以，当你有能力离开传统职业时，突然之间，各种其他的机会往往会以意想不到的方式冒出来。

turns.en: So Jessica, I'm curious, do you think about, you know, ever possibly going back to work or do you think that people who do retire early should sort of keep a toe in the working world to give themselves options if they do want to go back to work 10 or 20 years down the line? Well, I'm not wanting to tell people what they should do.
turns.zh: Jessica，我很好奇：你有没有想过以后某天可能回去工作？或者说，你觉得提前退休的人是不是应该在职业世界里留一只脚尖，给自己留个选项，万一10年、20年后又想回去工作呢？嗯，我并不想告诉别人应该怎么做。

turns.en: I think it's your life. You make whatever decisions feel good for you. I also will say that somebody who has walked this path who has retired early, and I always say retired early in quotes because to me, that doesn't mean you never work again. You never make a paycheck.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是你的人生，你做什么决定，只要自己觉得好就行。我还要说，一个走过这条路、已经提前退休的人——我说“提前退休”永远是加引号的，因为对我来说，那并不意味着你从此再也不工作、再也挣不到工资，

turns.en: It just means maybe you stepped away from the main source of income in the most recent years of your life. But anybody who has achieved this is, in my definition, hardworking, disciplined, driven, pretty exceptional. And so you're going to find something to keep you busy and to keep you productive.
turns.zh: 它只是意味着，也许你在人生最近的这些年里，从主要的收入来源上抽身了。但任何做到这一点的人，按我的定义，都是勤奋、自律、有驱动力、相当出色的人。所以你总会找到点什么事，让自己保持忙碌、保持产出。

turns.en: I mean, I just don't see a world where somebody who achieves financial independence is then happy sitting at home all day eating bond bonds and watching TV. Those two just don't equal in my brain. So if you want to keep your toe in the job market, I don't see why not.
turns.zh: 我是说，我实在想象不出这样的画面：一个实现了财务独立的人，然后心满意足地整天坐在家里吃糖果、看电视。这两件事在我脑子里就是画不上等号。所以，如果你想在就业市场里留一只脚尖，我觉得没什么不可以。

turns.en: And I'm sure that looks different depending on what career you walked away from. I have no desire to ever go back into sales. I've no desire to ever go back into corporate America. turns.zh: 而且我相信，这因人而异，取决于你离开的是什么职业。我毫无欲望再回去做销售，也毫无欲望再回到美国企业界。但“永不说不”，说不定我明天就改主意了。别人可能有一份不同的职业，也许他们会想回去。

turns.en: And sure, if that's something that speaks to you now, keep those doors open, keep those bridges up and sturdy and keep fostering those relationships that you've built. But yeah, I just don't know that that's something that somebody who has walked this path successfully
turns.zh: 当然，如果那是现在仍然吸引你的东西，那就把那些门留着，把桥保住、修得结结实实，继续维护你已经建立起来的人脉关系。不过，是的，我只是不觉得，一个成功走完这条路的人

turns.zh: 真的需要为此太担心，因为我觉得，如果你想工作，或者想让自己的时间过得有产出——无论是回到原来的职业、找一份新职业，甚至只是找一个可以全身心投入的爱好——我认为你

turns.zh: 在这条路上展现出的勤勉说明，一旦你想清楚了自己想要什么样的生活，你完全有能力按自己的意愿把时间填满。那么看起来，你们两位在很多方面高度一致：工作期间瞄准高储蓄率，聚焦于指数基金（index funds），或者说美国全市场指数基金。

turns.en: I'm curious, are there any areas where you disagree on how to approach financial matters? Absolutely not. It's funny because somebody else asked me this question recently and I thought about it for a few seconds and I said, we'll know because in full transparency, the topic of finances
turns.zh: 我很好奇，在处理财务问题的方式上，你们有没有什么分歧的地方？绝对没有。有意思的是，最近也有人问过我这个问题，我想了几秒钟，然后说：“没有。”因为坦白讲，财务这个话题

turns.en: not something that I enjoy and there has never been a part of me at any point in my life that thought, maybe I'll go research something else or maybe I'll go down a rabbit hole of a different strategy. I've just, I've never been interested in. So there is nothing financially related that dad and I disagree on a lot of stuff as
turns.zh: 并不是我享受的东西，而且在我人生的任何阶段，我内心都从来没有冒出过这样的念头：“也许我去研究点别的”，或者“也许我去钻研一下另一种策略”。我就是从来没兴趣。所以在财务相关的事情上，我和爸爸没有任何分歧——当然在很多别的事情上我们分歧不少，

When it comes to finances, no, we agree on everything purely because this is just what I grew up with and I never had an interest or a desire to even consider something other than what I was raised on. I don't know. Can you think of something? Like you said, when it comes to investing, we are well aligned.
turns.zh: 那就是另一个话题了。但在财务上，没有，我们什么都一致，纯粹因为这就是我从小长大的环境里的那一套，我从没有兴趣、也没有欲望去考虑任何别的路子。我想不出来，你能想到什么吗？就像你说的，在投资这件事上，我们高度一致。

turns.en: There are any number of other subjects. We're not so much, but yeah, I think, you know, Jess is, I tell her her superpower is she's never going to be tempted to tinker with what the simple path to wealth calls for because she is not interested in it. The simple path was designed for people like her who know that it's important.
turns.zh: 而在无数其他话题上，我们就没那么一致了。不过，是的，我觉得 Jess——我跟她说过，她的超能力就在于：她永远不会忍不住去改动 The Simple Path to Wealth 所要求的东西，因为她对此根本不感兴趣。“简单路径”本来就是为像她这样的人设计的：他们知道这件事很重要，

turns.zh: 知道把钱的事搞对了人生会更好，但他们其实对投资不感兴趣，也不想时时刻刻惦记它。这就是为什么它叫“通往财富的简单路径”。你只需要理解几个基本概念——她现在对这些理解得非常好——然后

turns.en: implement a couple of very simple strategies and then you're done and the less you tinker, the better you will do. It's really gratifying to me to see because I think of all the people that I've met over the last 15 years and talked to about this stuff.
turns.zh: 执行几个非常简单的策略，之后就完事了；你越少修修补补，效果就越好。看到这一点真的让我很欣慰，因为想想过去15年里我遇到并聊过这些话题的所有人，

turns.en: I think Jessica has followed the simple path to wealth in its purest form of anybody else. Almost everybody else is, wow, this is great and this is wonderful, but and then they tinker with it a little bit and she's never done that and she's gotten the stellar result. I think because of it that she hasn't tinkered with it.
turns.zh: 我认为 Jessica 是所有人当中以最纯粹的形式践行 The Simple Path to Wealth 的人。几乎所有人都是：“哇，这太棒了，这太好了，不过……”然后他们就动手改一点点；而她从来没有那样做，也因此得到了出色的结果——我认为正是因为她没有去瞎折腾。

turns.en: Yeah, I think that's a great point that investing in personal finance is probably one of the few areas of life where lack of interest is a big advantage.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得这个观点很棒：投资和个人理财，可能是生活中为数不多的“缺乏兴趣反而是巨大优势”的领域之一。

turns.en: As long as you get a couple of basic things right, you know, yeah. So Jessica, we often hear people giving the advice that you should spend money on experiences instead of things, but you write in the book that you think that's actually one of the biggest myths in personal finance. Can you discuss that a bit?
turns.zh: 只要你把几件基本的事情做对就行。那么 Jessica，我们经常听到有人建议：钱应该花在体验上，而不是物质上；但你在书里写道，你认为这其实是个人理财中最大的迷思之一。能展开讲讲吗？

turns.en: So I don't think there's a myth in spending your money on experiences over things. I actually, that's how I spend my money. I would much rather spend my money on experiences over things. That's how my parents spend their money. That's what I saw. That's how I was raised.
turns.zh: 我并不觉得“把钱花在体验而非物质上”本身是个迷思。实际上，我自己就是这么花钱的：与其买东西，我更愿意把钱花在体验上。我父母就是这么花钱的，这是我从小看到的，也是我成长的方式。

turns.en: The myth that I'm trying to bust is I guess it's not even a myth. It's this idea that when you're walking the path, it's a path of deprivation, right? And so what I'm trying to get across with the workbook and my ultimate goal is I don't care what you spend your money on.
turns.zh: 我想打破的那个迷思是——好吧，它甚至算不上迷思——而是这样一种观念：当你走这条路时，它是一条“克扣自己”的路，对吧？所以我在练习册里想传达的东西、我的终极目标是：我根本不在乎你把钱花在什么上。

turns.en: Like I said earlier, I'm not here to should anybody. You spend your money, whatever you want. You might read the workbook or somebody might read the workbook and say actually I have done these exercises. I feel very clear about my relationship with money and where I want to spend my
turns.zh: 就像我前面说的，我不是来对任何人指手画脚、告诉他们“应该”怎样的。你的钱，你想怎么花就怎么花。你读了这本练习册，或者别人读了之后可能会说：“其实我做过这些练习了，我对自己和金钱的关系、对我想把钱花在哪儿，已经非常清楚，

turns.en: money. And this path doesn't feel right for me. And that's cool. I am a okay with that because it's your money and your life. So what I really want my goal, what I was trying to get across is that you can spend your money on whatever you want. Just make sure you understand the why behind it.
turns.zh: 而这条路对我来说并不合适。”那也完全没问题，我 OK，因为那是你的钱、你的人生。所以我真正想要的、我想传达的目标是：你可以把钱花在任何你想要的东西上，只要确保你理解背后的“为什么”。

turns.en: And I think the conversation around experiences over objects or things is kind of not a necessary one because at the end of the day, you're still spending money and that's money that is going somewhere. turns.zh: 而且我觉得，关于“体验 vs 物品”的讨论其实没有太大必要，因为说到底，你都是在花钱，钱总是流向某处。这笔钱有机会成本（opportunity cost），它本可以用来投资，

turns.en: or saving for your future, buying your freedom. All that I am hoping that readers can figure out and gain clarity around is what do you actually want? What do you want to spend your money on? If you would rather spend your money on experiences, which like I said is what I do,
turns.zh: 或者为未来储蓄、“买回你的自由”。我只希望读者能够想清楚、获得清晰的认知：你到底想要什么？你想把钱花在什么上？如果你更愿意把钱花在体验上——就像我说的，我自己就是这样——

turns.en: that's fine. And from an emotional point of view, I 100% relate to that. If you would rather spend your money on things, that's okay too. But I think it's important to understand that if you are spending your money on a very expensive thing or if you're spending your money on a lot
turns.zh: 那没问题，而且从情感上讲，我百分之百能共鸣。如果你更愿意把钱花在物品上，那也 OK。但我觉得很重要的一点是要明白：如果你把钱花在一件非常昂贵的东西上，或者花在很多很多东西上，

turns.en: of things, that money cannot go towards your freedom. And so then when you have conversations with people who say, all the simple path to wealth is I know what I have to do, but it just feels so difficult and I can't do it. Well, now you know why because we know where our money is going.
turns.zh: 那这笔钱就没法流向你的“自由”了。所以当你和一些人聊，他们说：“The Simple Path to Wealth 里讲的我都知道该怎么做，可就是觉得太难了，我做不到。”那么现在你知道为什么了——因为我们都清楚自己的钱流向了哪里。

turns.en: I think another way to think about that is there is nothing magically more noble about spending money on experiences than on things. It's a matter of personal preference, not everybody like the class experience, of course, is travel. Well, not everybody enjoys travel, not everybody finds
turns.zh: 我觉得另一种思考方式是：把钱花在体验上，并没有什么 magically 更高尚之处，这纯粹是个人偏好。不是每个人都喜欢——当然，最经典的体验就是旅行。可并不是每个人都享受旅行，不是每个人都觉得旅行

turns.en: satisfying or desirable. And just because Jess and I happen to, it doesn't mean that's the right thing for everybody else. So whether you spend $10,000 on an amazing trip or $10,000 on remodeling your kitchen, there's nothing inherently more noble or better about one over the other is just
turns.zh: 令人满足或向往。仅仅因为 Jess 和我恰好喜欢，也不代表对其他人来说那就是对的事。所以，无论你是花1万美元来一趟美妙的旅行，还是花1万美元改造厨房，两者之间本质上没有谁更高尚、谁更好，只是

turns.en: said you're still making a choice to spend money and there's an opportunity cost to that. But as I've also said, you know, every decision doesn't have to be driven by the money, but you should understand the financial impact of those decisions.
turns.zh: 像刚才说的，你终究是在做一个花钱的选择，而这有机会成本。但我也说过，不是每一个决定都必须由钱来驱动，只是你应该理解这些决定在财务上的影响。
